newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops fortify captured northern areas.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops fortify captured northern areas.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops were fortifying positions in areas captured after fierce artillery and air attacks from Tamil Tiger rebels over the weekend, military officials in the north said in Monday.
They said security forces were building bunkers and forward defence lines north and northeast of government-held Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

Troops wrestled control of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya and northeastern Nedunkeni from Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels after the government launched its latest offensive, codenamed "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", last week.
"More security personnel have been sent to these areas to secure the places taken by the military," one official said.
Intelligence and police sources said the battle front was relatively quiet on Monday after last week's bierce fighting.

A Defence Ministry spokesman said on Sunday that some 250 rebels had been killed since the offensive began and that two divisions were moving on separate flanks, trying to open a land supply route linking Vvuniya with Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.

Troops backed by tanks, artillery and air cover on Saturday secured the town of Omanthai and are now pushing further north towards the heavily fortified rebel-held town of Puliyankulam, military officials said.
Rebel-controlled Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vuvuniya, fell to the army on Saturday after three days of fierce f)ghting.
"Troops are consolidating their positions in Nedunkeni and north of Omanthai," spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters on Sunday.
"We estimate about 250 terrorists have been killed in the operation," he added. "Enemy transmissions monitored by the army indicate 316 cadres have been wounded."
The rebels have accused the army of killing Tamil civilians and destroying property under the pretext of opening up a supply route, and of routinely exaggerating rebel casualties.
According to figures released by the army, 42 soldiers have been killed so far in the offensive. But newspaper reports put the toll at 70, including some officers.
Hospital sources said some 320 soldiers have been wounded.

The Defence Ministry has only said the main aim of the drive was to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni from the Tamil Tigers, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored by Reuters, said on Monday that the Sri Lankan navy had increased patrolling in the Palk Straits, which separates the island from India.

It said the army was still firing shells in the Wanni region and fighting was continuing. "Nedunkni has become a ghost town after virtually all Tamil residents -- now homeless -- were bombed out of their houses by persistent air and ground attacks", an overnight LTTE statement said.
Civilians who fled Nedunkeni said the army shelled rebel positions in the area for almost a week.
Journalists have not yet been allowed in the battle zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have dieD in the war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
